extracted.intended_audience: humor writers submitting short pieces to McSweeney's Internet Tendency
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short humor/satire pieces (lists, open letters, monologues, etc.) to McSweeney's Internet Tendency, including formatting, length, where to send different categories, and common rejection/anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send to correct submission address
rubrics_metrics.description: General website submissions should be sent to [email protected]; timely submissions to [email protected]; lists to [email protected]; open letters to [email protected]; Reviews of New Food to [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the inbox specific to the type of piece. If unsure, pick one — it all goes to the same editor. Do not send the same piece to multiple submission addresses simultaneously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely submissions (mark TIMELY)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely submissions are for super topical pieces riffing on big news stories of the day — stuff that HAS to run in the next day or else risk losing relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark the subject field as “TIMELY,” explain why the piece is super timely, and include a link to a reputable news site for proof. Note: submissions sent on Friday afternoons (EST) or over the weekend will be replied to the following Monday (on Tuesday after three-day weekends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists submissions address and handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists submissions have a dedicated inbox ([email protected]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists are accepted but are subject to the single-outstanding-submission rule; previously allowed up to three lists at a time, but now that is enforced as one at a time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open letters guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Open Letters to People or Entities Who Are Unlikely to Respond submissions should be sent to [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site generally publishes nonfiction letters that are written and signed by the submitter. They note they are all set for letters about noisy neighbors, small animals/insects that have invaded your living space, and breaking up with inanimate objects (e.g., Facebook, iPhones).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviews of New Food submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews of New Food should be sent to [email protected].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Currently they cannot pay for New Food Reviews; that may change if Patreon goals are met in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: No AI-assisted writing
rubrics_metrics.description: McSweeney's accepts no writing aided in any manner by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before publishing any writing— from a letter to a book-length work — authors published at McSweeney’s will be asked to attest that AI played no part in the creation or writing of that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not send to multiple addresses simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: Sending the same submission to multiple of the listed inboxes is unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions go to the same editor; if unsure which address to use, pick one. Multiple simultaneous sends are discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: No pitches — send completed drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitches are discouraged; submit only completed drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They explicitly request completed pieces rather than query/pitch emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be shortish: an absolute maximum of 1,200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They veer toward pieces under 1,000 words and prefer even shorter pieces when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author byline and contact info format
rubrics_metrics.description:
Your name should be on your submission under the title in this format: My Funny Experience [story title]
By William Williams [author’s name]
[email protected] [email address]
@wilywill [social handles].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the email address you want linked to your byline and any social handles you want shown; if you do not want them linked, tell the editor. Do not use an all-caps title; do not title the piece “My Funny Experience” as a joke (overused).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line should indicate content
rubrics_metrics.description: The email subject line should contain an indicator of what is contained in your submission (a version of the title is recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid subject lines like YOU’RE GOING TO LOVE THIS, INCREASE INCHES AND ENERGY TODAY, or INVITATION TO LINKEDIN. Be descriptive and professional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letters optional and short
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover letters are unnecessary but not forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If included, keep them very short — longer than three and a half sentences have a fair chance of not being read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paste the submission into the email body; no attachments or links
rubrics_metrics.description: Please paste the entire document into the email message; do not share Google Docs or links to private blogs and do not send attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editors are afraid of what attachments may be carrying. Putting text directly in the email body is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only one outstanding submission at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting one thing at a time is now strictly enforced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you receive a response about your current submission, you may send another one immediately. This rule also applies to lists submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting guidelines — keep it simple
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not format your piece in an unusual way (no colors or fun fonts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not describe how your piece would be best formatted — the site probably cannot achieve special formatting. Avoid clever formatting that renders text illegible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title importance and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles should quickly lure readers in and cleverly reveal the premises of pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor is drawn to funny, eye-catching titles that reveal premise (good examples: “I Regret to Inform You That My Wedding to Captain Von Trapp Has Been Canceled”; bad examples: “A Phone Call” or “Rabbits”). Avoid clickbait-y, all-caps list-style titles.

rubrics_metrics.name: No previously published work
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously published work cannot be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes material that has appeared on blogs, tumblrs, or sandwich boards. Do not send links to funny things on your blog/Tumblr/etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be payment for accepted general, open letter, and lists submissions (modest). You retain rights to your work after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is modest and depends on Patreon fundraising goals being met. Published work will be housed in their internet archives in perpetuity and they may re-post a link on social media from time to time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Average response time is 7.39 days; lists, open letters, and new food submissions often take longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses may be shorter and vaguer than submitters would like due to small editorial staff. If you haven’t heard within the indicated time frame, resend — a resend is often faster to handle than a query.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible technical/non-editorial reasons for no reply
rubrics_metrics.description: You might not hear back because of spam-blocking software, accidental deletion by the editor, or your own spam filter rejecting the reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam filters and resend if appropriate. The guideline lists humorous phrasing for these possibilities but the practical actions are checking spam settings and resending.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you don't hear back: resend
rubrics_metrics.description: If you don’t hear back within the stated time, resend your submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They explicitly say resending takes less time to respond to than answering a query; also feel free to vent to friends (humorous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Features that may harm your chances (anti-patterns)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of submission types and features that do not necessarily disqualify but do not help one’s cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes: poetry; book reviews; short stories; personal essays; submissions sent to multiple publications or undisclosed recipients; submissions formatted like news articles; submissions over the word limit; use of phrases like “these days” or “nowadays”; pieces that 'did not take place in a jungle' (humorous); containing more than 1.79 ironic exclamation points; not capitalizing first letters of sentences; not credited to a person with a first and last name; credited to an obvious pseudonym; clever formatting that renders it illegible; subject matter similar to something they've published recently; list of goofy email names from spam you received; submissions about being rejected by a humor website; bucket lists of different types of actual buckets; Christmas-themed pieces in the middle of May; riffs/sequels to another McSweeney’s piece you did not write; any piece that includes the word “McSweeney’s” in the title and/or text (they don't run stuff that references them).
